title: Platform systems & services: playbook, dashboards, runbooks, and roadmap
author: Priya Kapoor
content:
Overview

This document is the canonical platform engineering playbook for Redwood Inference's Platform Systems & Services team. It consolidates system descriptions, operational runbooks, dashboard and alert standards, recurring how-tos, recent retrospective outcomes, and the near-term roadmap. The intended audience is oncall engineers, platform SREs, product engineers integrating with platform services, and managers responsible for capacity and reliability.

Goals
- Provide a single reference for system owners and oncall responders.
- Reduce mean time to detection (MTTD) and mean time to recovery (MTTR) through clear runbooks and dashboards.
- Align roadmap priorities with reliability and cost targets.

Ownership and scope
- Primary owner: eng-platform (Platform Systems & Services).
- Secondary stakeholders: eng-infra (capacity & GPU fleet), eng-sre (SLOs & incident reviews), eng-serving-runtime (service contracts).
- Included services: routing-proxy, request-gateway, batching-engine, kv-cache, model-proxy, metrics-collector, billing-pipeline, alerting-proxy.

Systems & Services (high-level)
1) routing-proxy (team: platform-networking)
- Purpose: request ingress, auth, rate limiting, topology-based routing.
- SLA: 99.95% availability, p95 request latency target <= 60ms (control plane only).
- Key owners: service_owner: platform-networking, pager: pagers/platform-networking.

2) request-gateway (team: platform-api)
- Purpose: lightweight fronting service that performs request normalization, initial validation and routing to batching-engine or model-proxy.
- Expected QPS: 30k at peak across hosted clusters.
- SLO: 99.9% successful responses, error budget monthly = 0.1%.

3) batching-engine (team: platform-batching)
- Purpose: manage dynamic batching to GPUs, maintain KV cache, coordinate prefix cache reuse.
- Safety thresholds: max_batch_size_by_model: gptx-8b=128, gptx-32b=64. See appendix for model table.

4) kv-cache (team: platform-cache)
- Purpose: prefix cache for repeated prompt prefixes, reduces tokens served to model.
- Eviction policy: LRU with per-tenant TTL 24h default (configurable).

Dashboards & Alerts (standards and a prioritized list)
Standards (what each dashboard must include)
- Owner, last_updated, dashboard purpose (one sentence).
- Top-level KPIs: availability, error rate, p50/p95/p99 latencies, request rate (RPS), CPU/GPU utilization, cache hit ratio, billing cost rate.
- Drilldowns: per-region and per-model variant panels.
- Links: runbooks & relevant ADRs.

Critical dashboards (already deployed)
- Platform Overview (dash_id: platform-overview-2026) — aggregate health of routing-proxy, request-gateway, batching-engine, and model-proxy.
- Inference Latency & Errors (inference-latency-2026) — p50/p95/p99 per model, tail latency by sequence length.
- Batching Efficiency (batching-eff-2026) — batch sizes distribution, batching latency, concurrency per-GPU.
- KV-Cache Metrics (kv-cache-2026) — hit ratio by tenant, eviction rate, memory pressure.
- Cost & Utilization (cost-util-2026) — GPU hours, instance types, per-model cost/unit.

Alerting policy (examples and thresholds)
- P0: Service down — if platform-overview `service_availability` < 99% for 5m -> P0 pager.
- P1: High error rate — if API error-rate (5xx) > 1% sustained for 10m OR sudden spike (>5x baseline) -> P1 pager.
- P1: Latency degradation — p95 latency > 2x SLO for 10m -> P1.
- P2: Batch starvation — batching_engine `batch_fill_time` > 300ms for 5m -> notify channel #platform-ops.
- P2: Cache pressure — kv-cache `eviction_rate` > 5000/min -> investigate.

Example alert rule (PromQL)
- name: request-gateway-high-error-rate
  expr: 
    sum(rate(request_gateway_http_requests_total{status=~"5.."}[5m])) / sum(rate(request_gateway_http_requests_total[5m])) > 0.01
  for: 10m
  severity: P1

Runbooks (incident playbooks)
General runbook format (always present at top of every service runbook)
- Impact assessment: how to determine blast radius and affected customers.
- Initial triage: quick commands and checks.
- Mitigation steps: rolling restarts, scaling, failover routes.
- Recovery & verification: traffic tests, synthetic checks.
- Postmortem checklist: owner, timeline, root cause hypothesis, corrective actions.

Runbook: request-gateway (summary)
- Detection: alert request-gateway-high-error-rate or p95 latency > threshold.
- Triage checklist:
  1. Confirm alert: grafana -> Inference Latency & Errors dashboard.
  2. Check recent deploys: ci-cd pipeline -> last successful deploy to request-gateway.
  3. Check logs: kubectl -n platform logs deploy/request-gateway --since=15m | grep ERROR.
  4. Check upstream: routing-proxy healthchecks and connectivity to batching-engine.
- Mitigation (if error-rate high):
  1. Roll traffic to fallback model variant using routing-proxy: curl -X POST https://admin-routing.internal/rollout -d '{"route":"fallback"}' (requires SRE sudo).
  2. If a config flag is suspected, rollback to previous config via config-store (see config ops section).
  3. If CPU saturation: scale out request-gateway replicas: kubectl scale deployment/request-gateway --replicas=+3.
  4. If persistent downstream errors: disable batching for affected model: kubectl annotate deployment/batching-engine disable-batching=true --overwrite.

Runbook: batching-engine (summary)
- Detection: alert batching_engine_batch_starvation or batch_fill_time spike.
- Quick checks: GPU utilization panels, queue depth (queues/batching_engine_pending), model-proxy health.
- Hot mitigation steps:
  1. Increase max_workers in batching-engine config (path: /etc/batching/config.yaml) and trigger rolling restart.
  2. Temporarily lower max_batch_size_by_model for high-seq models to free GPU memory.
  3. Enable burst-mode autoscale (policy: burst-on-high-queue) for the affected cluster.

How-tos (common procedures)
- Adding a new dashboard: copy `dashboard-template.json`, update metadata (owner, panels, links to runbooks), and open PR to `infra/grafana-dashboards` repo. Reviewer: dashboards@redwood.com.
- Oncall handover: update the oncall sheet, post current pager items in #platform-ops-handover, and run `make /scripts/export-oncall-summary` to publish summary.
- Performing a hotfix release: follow CI/CD hotfix playbook: tag release vX.Y.Z-hotfix, run `./scripts/hotfix-deploy.sh request-gateway`, validate with the smoke test suite.

Retrospectives (recent outcomes & improvements)
- Q4 2025 platform incident retrospective (INC-2025-11-18) highlights:
  - Root cause: regression in batching-engine request partitioning after model-proxy client update.
  - Actions: preflight test added to CI for batching-model-compat, increased integration-test coverage by 40%, introduced synthetic canary for batching-engine.
  - Status: 3/4 actions completed, last action (cataloging model-compat flags) due 2026-03-15.
- Postmortem hygiene improvements: all P0/P1 postmortems now have a labeled action owner and due date in the ticketing system.

Roadmap (next 6 months, prioritized)
- Q1–Q2 2026 priorities:
  1. Platform observability expansion — add per-tenant cost panels and model-level tokenization breakdown (owner: eng-platform, target: 2026-04-30).
  2. Batching engine resilience improvements — preallocation and smarter backpressure (owner: eng-serving-runtime + platform-batching, target: 2026-06-15).
  3. KV-cache eviction tuning & multi-tenant QoS — implement configurable eviction windows and per-tenant quotas (owner: platform-cache, target: 2026-05-31).
  4. Alerting rationalization — reduce noise by consolidating 42 alerts into 12 high-signal rules (owner: eng-sre, target: 2026-04-15).
  5. Onprem runbook package — canonical runbooks for Private deployments (owner: eng-private-deployments, target: 2026-06-30).

Team Wiki & References (quick links)
- Team wiki home: /confluence/eng-platform/platform-team-wiki-and-runbooks-2026
- Grafana repo: git@git.redwood:infra/grafana-dashboards.git
- Alerts repo: git@git.redwood:infra/alerting-rules.git
- Runbooks directory: /confluence/eng-platform/runbooks/index

Operational play: escalation matrix
1. Pager (P0/P1): primary oncall in PagerDuty for platform-sre. If no response in 5m escalate to secondary and notify Eng Manager.
2. Legal/compliance: if incident includes customer data exposure, immediately inform Security & Compliance and legal (see security-and-compliance/contact-list).

Appendix A — common commands
- Check routing-proxy pods: kubectl -n platform get pods -l app=routing-proxy -o wide
- Tail request-gateway logs: kubectl -n platform logs deploy/request-gateway -f --since=1h
- Trigger Grafana alert test: curl -X POST https://grafana.internal/api/alerts/test --header 'Authorization: Bearer <token>'

Appendix B — model table (excerpt)
| model_variant | max_batch_size | recommended_sequence_cutoff | owner_team |
| gptx-8b | 128 | 1024 | eng-serving-runtime |
| gptx-32b | 64 | 2048 | eng-serving-runtime |

Appendix C — config locations and important files
- /etc/platform/config.yaml (global config)
- s3://redwood-configs/platform/batching/config.yaml (batching config by cluster)
- infra/helm/charts/request-gateway/values.yaml (deployment values)

Contact & escalation owners
- Platform lead: Priya Kapoor (priya.kapoor@redwood.com)
- SRE lead: Daniel Park (daniel.park@redwood.com)
- Oncall rotation: see PagerDuty: Redwood Platform SRE schedule

Change log
- 2026-02-28: Published initial consolidated playbook and updated alert thresholds for batching-engine.
- 2025-11-15: Draft created and reviewed by platform leads.

Next steps
- Maintain this doc alongside dashboards and runbooks. Engineers should add or update runbooks after any action that changes operational behavior (deploys, config changes, rollout policies).
summary: Canonical playbook for Platform Systems & Services: includes systems descriptions, dashboard and alert standards, runbooks, retrospectives, and roadmap.
